lessons.title: A railway works side becomes United
lessons.subtitle: Newton Heath’s long road to a new name

story.title: A team from the works
story.body: Workers at the Lancashire and Yorkshire Railway depot in Newton Heath formed a football team in 1878. The club entered the Football League in 1892 as Newton Heath.

story.title: A name and a first title
story.body: After financial collapse, new investment and a new identity came in 1902. The club then won its first league championship in 1907/08.

facts.label: League entry level
facts.prompt: At which division level did Newton Heath enter the Football League in 1892?
facts.scope: Newton Heath’s 1892 entry into the Football League.
facts.evidence: Manchester United’s official history says Newton Heath joined the Football League at Division One level in 1892.

facts.label: Name change
facts.prompt: In what year was the Manchester United name adopted after the club was saved from extinction?
facts.scope: The club’s formal change from Newton Heath to Manchester United.
facts.evidence: The club chronology says John Henry Davies invested in the financially troubled Newton Heath and Manchester United was born in April/May 1902.

facts.label: First league championship
facts.prompt: Which season brought Manchester United its first league championship?
facts.scope: The first Football League championship won under the Manchester United name.
facts.evidence: The club’s 1878–1909 history records its first league title in 1907/08.

lessons.title: The Babes’ last match on English soil
lessons.subtitle: A nine-goal Highbury classic before Munich

story.title: A remarkable afternoon
story.body: On 1 February 1958, Manchester United beat Arsenal at Highbury in front of 63,578 spectators. The official club history calls it the team’s greatest game on English soil.

story.title: The last journey
story.body: The Busby Babes left Highbury for the European Cup tie in Belgrade. Their flight home stopped in Munich, where the crash killed players, staff and others connected with the club.

facts.label: Opponent
facts.prompt: Which London club did United beat at Highbury in the Babes’ final match on English soil?
facts.scope: Manchester United’s final game in England before the Munich air disaster.
facts.evidence: The club’s history names Arsenal as the opponent at Highbury on 1 February 1958.

facts.label: Highbury attendance
facts.prompt: How many spectators watched the 1 February 1958 Highbury match?
facts.scope: Attendance at the 5–4 match against Arsenal.
facts.evidence: The club history gives the crowd as 63,578.

facts.label: Nine-goal match
facts.prompt: How many goals were scored in the Highbury match that United won before travelling to Belgrade?
facts.scope: Combined goals in United’s 5–4 win at Arsenal.
facts.evidence: The official club account describes the 5–4 game as a nine-goal thriller.

lessons.title: Van Persie seals the twentieth
lessons.subtitle: A hat-trick settled the title at Old Trafford

story.title: Title night
story.body: United hosted Aston Villa on 22 April 2013 knowing a win would secure the Premier League. Robin van Persie scored all three in a 3–0 victory.

story.title: A landmark crown
story.body: The result gave United its 20th English league championship, four matches before the season ended.

facts.label: Match date
facts.prompt: On what date did United clinch the 2012/13 title by beating Aston Villa?
facts.scope: The decisive Premier League match at Old Trafford.
facts.evidence: Manchester United’s match page dates the 3–0 Villa win to 22 April 2013.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was Manchester United’s score against Aston Villa when it clinched the Premier League title on 22 April 2013?
facts.scope: Manchester United v Aston Villa, 22 April 2013.
facts.evidence: The official match title and highlights give the result as United 3, Aston Villa 0.

facts.label: Hat-trick scorer
facts.prompt: Which United player scored the hat-trick that night?
facts.scope: Manchester United’s title-clinching home win over Aston Villa.
facts.evidence: The club states that Robin van Persie scored the hat-trick on the night United were crowned champions for a 20th time.

lessons.title: A teenage signing makes an instant impact
lessons.subtitle: Rooney’s first United season

story.title: A major move
story.body: Rooney joined Manchester United from Everton in 2004, choosing the club after interest from other teams. He arrived as an 18-year-old forward with a reputation already built in English football.

story.title: Goals straight away
story.body: His United debut included a Champions League hat-trick. He added 14 more goals that season and ended 2004/05 as the team’s leading scorer with 17.

facts.label: Transfer year
facts.prompt: In what year did Wayne Rooney sign for Manchester United from Everton?
facts.scope: Rooney’s transfer from Everton to Manchester United.
facts.evidence: Rooney’s United podcast says he signed in 2004 and discusses his decision to choose the club.

facts.label: Age at transfer
facts.prompt: How old was Rooney when he joined United in 2004?
facts.scope: Rooney’s age when he moved to Manchester United.
facts.evidence: United’s 2004 unveiling video identifies Rooney as 18 when he signed; its signing feature confirms the 2004 transfer.

facts.label: First-season total
facts.prompt: How many goals did Rooney score in all competitions for United in 2004/05?
facts.scope: Rooney’s total United goals in his first season, including his debut hat-trick.
facts.evidence: The United podcast says he added 14 after his debut treble to finish as the team’s prime marksman with 17.

story.title: A first appearance
story.body: Rooney made his Manchester United debut against Fenerbahçe in the Champions League on 28 September 2004. He scored three times in a 6–2 win.

story.title: A statement entrance
story.body: He became the first player to score a hat-trick on a United European debut. A late free-kick completed the treble, immediately announcing his arrival to the home crowd.

facts.label: Debut date
facts.prompt: When did Rooney make his Manchester United debut against Fenerbahçe?
facts.scope: Rooney’s first appearance for United, against Fenerbahçe in the Champions League.
facts.evidence: The official United match feature identifies 28 September 2004 as Rooney’s debut and hat-trick match.

facts.label: Match result
facts.prompt: What was the final score in Rooney’s Champions League debut against Fenerbahçe?
facts.scope: Manchester United versus Fenerbahçe, Rooney’s 2004 debut match.
facts.evidence: UEFA identifies the match as Manchester United 6–2 Fenerbahçe.

facts.label: Debut scoring feat
facts.prompt: How many goals did Rooney score in that first United appearance?
facts.scope: Rooney’s Champions League debut against Fenerbahçe.
facts.evidence: UEFA says Rooney scored a debut hat-trick and describes the free-kick that completed it.

story.title: A vital derby
story.body: On 12 February 2011, United beat Manchester City 2–1 at Old Trafford. Rooney’s acrobatic strike came from Nani’s deflected cross and proved the winner.

story.title: A landmark goal
story.body: The victory helped United on the way to a 19th league title. Rooney’s overhead kick became one of the defining goals of the Premier League era.

facts.label: Derby opponent
facts.prompt: Which local rival did United beat when Rooney scored his famous overhead kick in 2011?
facts.scope: United’s 2–1 Old Trafford win on 12 February 2011.
facts.evidence: The official United match retrospective identifies the goal as Rooney’s effort against Manchester City.

facts.label: Derby score
facts.prompt: What was the score in the 2011 Manchester derby decided by Rooney’s overhead kick?
facts.scope: Manchester United v Manchester City at Old Trafford, 12 February 2011.
facts.evidence: The club’s account calls it a 2–1 United win.

facts.label: Goal technique
facts.prompt: What kind of strike did Rooney use for his winning goal against City?
facts.scope: Rooney’s winning goal in the 2011 Manchester derby.
facts.evidence: United’s goal retrospective explicitly describes the effort as an overhead kick.

story.title: The record falls
story.body: Rooney’s goal at Stoke on 21 January 2017 was his 250th for Manchester United. It moved him past Sir Bobby Charlton as the club’s all-time leading scorer.

story.title: A lasting total
story.body: He finished his United career with 253 goals in 559 appearances, a scoring record built across 13 seasons at Old Trafford.

facts.label: Milestone date
facts.prompt: When did Rooney score his record-breaking 250th goal for United?
facts.scope: Rooney’s 250th goal for Manchester United, scored at Stoke City.
facts.evidence: The Premier League dates the event to 21 January 2017 and reports that his 250th United goal made him the club’s record scorer.

facts.label: Career goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Rooney score in his 559 Manchester United appearances?
facts.scope: Rooney’s completed Manchester United career total.
facts.evidence: The Professional Footballers’ Association records Rooney’s departure in 2017 with 253 goals in 559 appearances for United.

facts.label: Previous record holder
facts.prompt: Whose club scoring record did Rooney pass to become United’s leading scorer?
facts.scope: Manchester United’s all-time goalscoring record before Rooney’s milestone.
facts.evidence: The Premier League states the 250th goal took Rooney above Sir Bobby Charlton for Manchester United.

story.title: A United debut
story.body: Paul Scholes came through Manchester United’s youth system and made his first-team debut at Port Vale on 21 September 1994, aged 19.

story.title: A return to the pitch
story.body: United’s official history places Scholes’s return in its 2011/12 season account. He ended his playing career for good in 2013.

facts.label: First-team debut
facts.prompt: On what date did Paul Scholes make his Manchester United debut at Port Vale?
facts.scope: Scholes’s senior debut for Manchester United in the League Cup.
facts.evidence: United’s academy debutants list gives 21 September 1994, Port Vale, age 19.

facts.label: Comeback season
facts.prompt: During which season did Scholes return to Manchester United after retirement?
facts.scope: Paul Scholes’s return to the United squad after retirement.
facts.evidence: United’s 2010 onwards history places his return in its narrative of the 2011/12 season.

facts.label: Final retirement
facts.prompt: In what year did Scholes end his playing career for good after returning to United?
facts.scope: Scholes’s final end to his playing career after returning to United.
facts.evidence: The Premier League Hall of Fame profile dates Scholes’s United playing career from 1994 through 2013.

lessons.title: A strike sends United to Moscow
lessons.subtitle: The 2008 semi-final against Barcelona

story.title: A tense second leg
story.body: After a goalless first leg in Barcelona, United hosted the return match on 29 April 2008. Scholes struck in the first half to give the home side a 1–0 win.

story.title: A place in the final
story.body: That goal settled the tie and sent United to the Champions League final, where they would face Chelsea in Moscow.

facts.label: Semi-final date
facts.prompt: On what date did Scholes score the goal that eliminated Barcelona in 2008?
facts.scope: The second leg of the 2007/08 Champions League semi-final.
facts.evidence: The official United match highlight labels the Barcelona 1–0 match as 29 April 2008.

facts.label: Second-leg score
facts.prompt: What was the score when United beat Barcelona at Old Trafford in the 2008 semi-final?
facts.scope: Manchester United v Barcelona, second leg of the 2008 Champions League semi-final.
facts.evidence: The official highlights are titled Man United 1 Barcelona 0.

facts.label: Tie outcome
facts.prompt: What did Scholes’s goal earn Manchester United against Barcelona?
answers: A place in the Champions League final
distractors: A place in the UEFA Cup final

value.display: A place in the Champions League final
value.text: A place in the Champions League final

facts.scope: The outcome of the 2008 Champions League semi-final tie.
facts.evidence: United’s account says Scholes’s strike sent United through to the Champions League final.

lessons.title: The Valley Parade volley
lessons.subtitle: Scholes turns a corner into a classic

story.title: A two-goal lead
story.body: United were already 2–0 up at Bradford City when Beckham took a corner. Scholes moved into space and met the delivery with a volley.

story.title: A four-goal win
story.body: The goal came in a 4–0 away victory on 25 March 2000, during United’s successful title defence.

facts.label: Corner taker
facts.prompt: Who delivered the corner that Scholes volleyed in the 2000 match at Bradford?
facts.scope: The set-piece that led to Scholes’s goal at Valley Parade.
facts.evidence: The official club feature says Beckham delivered the corner before Scholes struck.

facts.label: Score before goal
facts.prompt: What was Manchester United’s score against Bradford immediately after Paul Scholes’s volley on 25 March 2000?
facts.scope: Match state before Scholes’s goal in United’s 4–0 win.
facts.evidence: The club retrospective says two Dwight Yorke goals had put United 2–0 ahead before the volley.

facts.label: Final result
facts.prompt: What was the final score of United’s away match at Bradford in March 2000?
facts.scope: Manchester United’s visit to Bradford City on 25 March 2000.
facts.evidence: United’s official feature records the final score as 4–0.

lessons.title: Service, scoring and silverware
lessons.subtitle: Scholes’s Premier League record and United goal total

story.title: A long United career
story.body: Scholes made 499 Premier League appearances for United and scored 107 league goals. The Premier League records those totals across his career in the competition.

story.title: Recognition beyond Old Trafford
story.body: Scholes won 11 Premier League titles with United, including a title after his return from retirement. He also scored 155 goals for the club in all competitions.

facts.label: Top-flight appearances
facts.prompt: How many Premier League appearances did Scholes make for Manchester United?
facts.scope: Scholes’s appearances in the Premier League, which are fewer than his all-competition appearances.
facts.evidence: The Premier League Hall of Fame profile gives Scholes 499 league appearances.

facts.label: Premier League titles
facts.prompt: How many Premier League titles did Scholes win with Manchester United over his career?
facts.scope: Scholes’s Premier League titles with United, including the title won after his 2011 retirement and 2012 return.
facts.evidence: The Premier League Hall of Fame profile says Scholes helped United to 11 Premier League titles.

facts.label: United goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Scholes score for Manchester United in all competitions?
facts.scope: Scholes’s Manchester United career total across competitions, not his Premier League-only total.
facts.evidence: Manchester United’s official goal clip calls the Port Vale debut strike the first of Scholes’s 155 United goals.

lessons.title: A club born in Vila-real
lessons.subtitle: Early decisions gave Villarreal its identity

story.title: The founding
story.body: A group of local football enthusiasts founded Club Deportivo Villarreal on 10 March 1923. Pharmacist José Calduch was among the club’s driving forces.

story.title: The first colours
story.body: The new club selected white shirts and black shorts for its first kits. Yellow shirts arrived in 1946 and became an enduring part of the club’s identity.

facts.label: Founding date
facts.prompt: On what date was Club Deportivo Villarreal founded?
facts.scope: Foundation of CD Villarreal, predecessor of Villarreal CF.
facts.evidence: The club’s foundation history dates CD Villarreal’s formation to 10 March 1923.

facts.label: Driving force
facts.prompt: Which local pharmacist was among the driving forces behind the founding of CD Villarreal?
facts.scope: The 1923 foundation of the club.
facts.evidence: Villarreal’s official history identifies pharmacist José Calduch as a leading founder and first president.

facts.label: Yellow shirts
facts.prompt: In what year did Villarreal’s shirts change from white to yellow?
facts.scope: The club’s shirt colour change from its original white and black kit.
facts.evidence: The club history says the original white shirts remained until 1946, when they changed to yellow.

lessons.title: Riquelme’s last-minute penalty
lessons.subtitle: Villarreal’s 2006 European run ends at the spot

story.title: A narrow deficit
story.body: Villarreal hosted Arsenal in the second leg of the 2005/06 Champions League semi-final on 25 April 2006, trailing 1–0 from London. The match remained goalless.

story.title: One final chance
story.body: In the 89th minute, Juan Román Riquelme took a penalty that could have levelled the aggregate score. Jens Lehmann saved it, and Arsenal advanced 1–0 on aggregate.

facts.label: Semi-final date
facts.prompt: On what date did Villarreal host Arsenal in the second leg of the 2006 Champions League semi-final?
facts.scope: Villarreal v Arsenal, second leg of the 2005/06 Champions League semi-final.
facts.evidence: UEFA dates the match report to Tuesday, 25 April 2006.

facts.label: Penalty taker
facts.prompt: Which Villarreal player took the 89th-minute penalty against Arsenal?
facts.scope: The late penalty in the second leg at El Madrigal.
facts.evidence: UEFA states Riquelme stepped up in the 89th minute and had his spot-kick saved.

facts.label: Aggregate result
facts.prompt: What was Villarreal’s aggregate score against Arsenal when the 2006 semi-final ended?
facts.scope: Villarreal’s aggregate result in the two-leg 2006 Champions League semi-final.
facts.evidence: UEFA reports Arsenal’s 1–0 first-leg win and a 0–0 second leg; Villarreal therefore lost 0–1 on aggregate.

lessons.title: Twenty-two kicks to a first European crown
lessons.subtitle: Rulli decides the 2021 final shoot-out

story.title: A final that stayed level
story.body: Villarreal and Manchester United drew 1–1 after extra time in Gdańsk on 26 May 2021. Gerard Moreno opened the scoring and Edinson Cavani equalised.

story.title: The goalkeeper decides it
story.body: After the first 20 penalties were converted, Gerónimo Rulli scored and then saved David de Gea’s attempt. Villarreal won the shoot-out 11–10 and its first major European trophy.

facts.label: Final date
facts.prompt: When did Villarreal beat Manchester United in the Europa League final?
facts.scope: The 2020/21 UEFA Europa League final in Gdańsk.
facts.evidence: UEFA dates the final to Wednesday, 26 May 2021.

facts.label: After extra time
facts.prompt: What was Villarreal’s score against Manchester United after extra time in the 2021 Europa League final?
facts.scope: Villarreal v Manchester United, before the penalty shoot-out.
facts.evidence: UEFA’s final report gives the match as 1–1 after extra time.

facts.label: Winning save
facts.prompt: Which goalkeeper saved the decisive Manchester United penalty in the shoot-out?
facts.scope: The 22nd penalty in the 2021 Europa League final shoot-out.
facts.evidence: UEFA says Rulli saved the 22nd kick from De Gea to give Villarreal the trophy.

story.title: A fresh start
story.body: Diego Forlán arrived at Villarreal from Manchester United in summer 2004. He quickly became the focal point of the attack and formed a strong partnership with Juan Román Riquelme.

story.title: Three prolific seasons
story.body: Forlán scored 59 goals in three seasons for Villarreal before moving to Atlético Madrid in summer 2007. His first campaign brought both a European scoring honour and a club scoring milestone.

facts.label: Previous club
facts.prompt: Which club did Forlán leave to join Villarreal in summer 2004?
facts.scope: Forlán’s arrival at Villarreal in 2004.
facts.evidence: Villarreal’s player retrospective says he signed from Manchester United in summer 2004.

facts.label: Seasons at Villarreal
facts.prompt: How many seasons did Forlán play for Villarreal before leaving in 2007?
facts.scope: Forlán’s Villarreal spell ending with his 2007 transfer.
facts.evidence: The club describes his transfer as occurring three years after his 2004 arrival, in summer 2007; this means three seasons with Villarreal.

facts.label: Next club
facts.prompt: Which club signed Forlán from Villarreal in summer 2007?
facts.scope: Forlán’s move after three Villarreal seasons.
facts.evidence: Villarreal reports it sold Forlán to Atlético Madrid in summer 2007.

lessons.title: Forlán strikes in Milan
lessons.subtitle: Forlán strikes at the Giuseppe Meazza

story.title: Quarter-final pressure
story.body: In the 2005/06 Champions League quarter-final against Inter, Forlán scored in the opening seconds at the Giuseppe Meazza. Villarreal’s official retrospective remembers the goal as coming after just 45 seconds.

story.title: A memorable away strike
story.body: It was one of two important goals Forlán scored during Villarreal’s run to the semi-finals that season, a campaign in which the club came close to reaching the final.

facts.label: Quarter-final opponent
facts.prompt: Which Italian club did Villarreal face when Forlán scored at the Giuseppe Meazza in 2006?
facts.scope: The 2005/06 Champions League quarter-final away leg.
facts.evidence: The club’s Forlán feature identifies the quarter-final opponent as Inter Milan.

facts.label: Stadium
facts.prompt: At which stadium did Forlán score his rapid quarter-final goal against Inter?
facts.scope: Villarreal’s away quarter-final match against Inter.
facts.evidence: The official account places the goal at the Giuseppe Meazza. Distractors are distinct stadiums; San Siro is treated as a synonym and therefore excluded below.

facts.label: Time to goal
facts.prompt: How soon did Forlán score at Inter’s stadium in that Champions League tie?
facts.scope: The opening phase of Villarreal’s 2005/06 quarter-final at Inter.
facts.evidence: Villarreal’s official retrospective says the goal came after just 45 seconds.

lessons.title: A hat-trick at Camp Nou
lessons.subtitle: Forlán’s first LaLiga treble for Villarreal

story.title: A statement away performance
story.body: Forlán scored his first LaLiga hat-trick for Villarreal at Camp Nou during the 2004/05 season. The match finished 3–3 against Barcelona.

story.title: A rare club mark
story.body: Villarreal’s Spanish profile identifies two LaLiga hat-tricks for Forlán: this 3–3 at Camp Nou in 2004/05 and another against Osasuna in 2006/07.

facts.label: Opponent
facts.prompt: Which team was Villarreal playing when Forlán scored his first LaLiga hat-trick for the club?
facts.scope: Forlán’s first Villarreal LaLiga hat-trick, played at Camp Nou.
facts.evidence: Villarreal’s Spanish profile names the first of Forlán’s two LaLiga hat-tricks as the 3–3 at Camp Nou.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was Barcelona’s score against Villarreal in Diego Forlán’s Camp Nou hat-trick match on 22 May 2005?
facts.scope: Villarreal’s 2004/05 LaLiga match at Barcelona.
facts.evidence: The Spanish official profile gives the Camp Nou match as 3–3.

facts.label: Season
facts.prompt: In which season did Forlán score that first Villarreal LaLiga hat-trick?
facts.scope: Forlán’s first LaLiga treble for Villarreal.
facts.evidence: The Spanish official profile dates Forlán’s first Villarreal LaLiga hat-trick to 2004/05.

lessons.title: Europe’s leading scorer
lessons.subtitle: A first-season scoring record and rare club mark

story.title: A prolific league campaign
story.body: Forlán scored 25 domestic goals in 2004/05, making him the top scorer across Europe that season. Villarreal’s retrospective calls this the campaign’s Golden Ball; the lesson focuses on the precise scoring record and the club’s stated hat-trick mark.

story.title: A lasting club mark
story.body: Across three seasons in yellow he scored 59 times. Villarreal’s Spanish profile says he was the only player in club history to score two LaLiga hat-tricks.

facts.label: Domestic goals
facts.prompt: How many domestic goals did Forlán score for Villarreal in the 2004/05 season?
facts.scope: Forlán’s 2004/05 domestic season for Villarreal.
facts.evidence: The club says his 25 domestic strikes made him the top scorer across the continent.

facts.label: LaLiga hat-tricks
facts.prompt: How many LaLiga hat-tricks did Forlán score for Villarreal, according to the club’s Spanish profile?
facts.scope: Forlán’s LaLiga hat-tricks for Villarreal, as described in the club’s retrospective.
facts.evidence: Villarreal’s Spanish-language official profile says Forlán was the only player in club history to score two Primera División hat-tricks, naming Camp Nou in 2004/05 and Osasuna in 2006/07. The English translation incorrectly says three.

facts.label: Villarreal goals
facts.prompt: How many goals did Forlán score in his three seasons at Villarreal?
facts.scope: Forlán’s completed Villarreal scoring total across three seasons.
facts.evidence: The club’s profile records 59 goals in his three seasons as a Yellow.

story.title: A Brazilian arrival
story.body: Marcos Senna joined Villarreal in summer 2002 from São Caetano. After overcoming two serious knee injuries early in his time at the club, he became a midfield cornerstone.

story.title: A club emblem
story.body: He wore Villarreal’s shirt for 11 seasons, captained the team and scored 33 goals despite playing as a holding midfielder.

facts.label: Arrival year
facts.prompt: In what year did Senna join Villarreal from São Caetano?
facts.scope: Senna’s transfer from São Caetano to Villarreal.
facts.evidence: Villarreal’s biography says Senna arrived in summer 2002 from São Caetano.

facts.label: Seasons in yellow
facts.prompt: How many seasons did Senna represent Villarreal?
facts.scope: Senna’s first-team tenure with Villarreal.
facts.evidence: The club says he wore the yellow shirt for 11 seasons.

facts.label: Goals as a midfielder
facts.prompt: How many goals did Senna score for Villarreal?
facts.scope: Senna’s goals for Villarreal, where he played as a holding midfielder.
facts.evidence: The official profile records 33 goals for the Yellows.

lessons.title: He stayed to help Villarreal rise again
lessons.subtitle: Senna’s response to relegation

story.title: A difficult fall
story.body: Villarreal dropped from the top flight after the 2011/12 season. Senna chose to extend his contract rather than leave and stayed for another season.

story.title: Back to Primera
story.body: The club returned to the top division after the 2012/13 campaign. Villarreal’s account remembers Senna as a committed leader who helped the team regain its place in the top flight.

facts.label: Relegation season
facts.prompt: After which season did Villarreal suffer the relegation that Senna stayed to respond to?
facts.scope: Villarreal’s drop to Segunda División before the promotion season.
facts.evidence: The club’s historical table shows Villarreal 18th in Primera in 2011/12; Senna’s profile says he stayed after relegation.

facts.label: Senna’s choice
facts.prompt: What did Senna decide to do after Villarreal were relegated?
answers: Extend his contract and stay another season

value.display: Extend his contract and stay another season
value.text: Extend his contract and stay another season

facts.scope: Senna’s decision after Villarreal went down to Segunda.
facts.evidence: The club says he extended his contract and stayed one more season to help return Villarreal to the top flight.

facts.label: Next club
facts.prompt: After Villarreal returned to the top flight, which club did Senna join to finish his playing career?
facts.scope: Senna’s move after he stayed one additional season and helped Villarreal return to the top flight.
facts.evidence: Villarreal says Senna left after the promotion season to end his career in the United States with New York Cosmos.

story.title: Across competitions
story.body: Senna played 363 official matches for Villarreal. That tally included 292 LaLiga matches and appearances in several European and domestic cups.

story.title: A benchmark in yellow
story.body: When Villarreal welcomed Senna back in 2015, the club described him as its record-holder for official appearances. His total remains 363, although the club later reported that Bruno Soriano surpassed the mark.

facts.label: Official appearances
facts.prompt: How many official matches did Senna play for Villarreal across competitions?
facts.scope: Senna’s total official Villarreal appearances at the time of the club’s tribute.
facts.evidence: The club lists 363 total official appearances and identifies him as the record holder at that time.

facts.label: League appearances
facts.prompt: How many of Senna’s Villarreal matches were in LaLiga?
facts.scope: Senna’s LaLiga appearances within his 363-match Villarreal total.
facts.evidence: The club breaks his appearances down and lists 292 in the Spanish first division.

facts.label: Champions League appearances
facts.prompt: How many Champions League matches did Senna play for Villarreal?
facts.scope: Senna’s Villarreal appearances in the UEFA Champions League.
facts.evidence: The club’s competition breakdown gives Senna 27 Champions League appearances.

lessons.title: From São Paulo to European champion
lessons.subtitle: Senna’s Spain international legacy

story.title: Spain career
story.body: Villarreal records 28 matches for Spain, including two at the 2006 World Cup. Senna made his national-team debut in 2006.

story.title: A European champion
story.body: Senna helped Spain win UEFA EURO 2008, a defining achievement in his international career.

facts.label: Spain appearances
facts.prompt: How many Spain appearances did Senna make while playing for Villarreal, according to the club’s 2019 count?
